summary: Partial streaming reconnect causes duplicate external webhook invocation when function-calls resume (Go SDK)
description:
Issue summary: BrightCart reports duplicate outbound webhook executions when a client reconnects to a partially-streamed response that included function/tool calls. Impact: Customers observed duplicate downstream side-effects (order webhook fired twice) after a network blip during streaming. This looks tied to the Go SDK reconnect behavior.

High level: customer initiated a streaming chat which invoked two sequential function calls (createOrder -> notifyFulfillment). Network dropped during the second function call's streaming chunk. The Go SDK automatically reconnected and resumed; the downstream webhook (notifyFulfillment) was observed and processed twice by the customer's fulfillment service.

Why this matters: duplicated side-effects are critical for BrightCart since notifyFulfillment triggers shipment processing. They are on Dedicated and require guidance and a remediation path.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use go-sdk v0.9.2 with streaming chat + function calling and a user session that triggers two function calls in sequence (createOrder then notifyFulfillment).
2) Start streaming response and allow the server to send first function call and partial second call payload (simulate large payload or delayed flush).
3) Introduce a brief TCP interruption (client-side network drop) while the second function payload is mid-stream, then allow the SDK to reconnect automatically.
4) Observe that the server emits the function call again after reconnect and the customer's webhook endpoint receives a duplicate POST shortly after the first one.
expected_behavior: After a transient reconnect during streaming, the function call should be delivered exactly once (at-most-once semantics) or the SDK should provide a stable idempotency key that the customer can use to deduplicate safely.
actual_behavior: Webhook notifyFulfillment is posted twice for the same logical function call when the client reconnects mid-stream. BrightCart reports both calls cause shipment events to be recorded, leading to duplicate shipments.

comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-01: Customer called in; says duplicate shipment created. They are on Dedicated and would like a temporary mitigation while engineering investigates.
BrightCart Engineering (customer) 2026-03-01: We see two identical POSTs within 2s. We attempted to dedupe on our side by request id header but the SDK had no stable header across reconnects.
Oliver Patel (SRE) 2026-03-02: Reproduced locally with go-sdk v0.9.2 using a TCP kill script. Observed behavior matches. Attaching pcap and server logs to GitHub issue.

Nora Ahmed (SDK Eng) 2026-03-02: Hypothesis: go-sdk v0.9.2 regenerates the session/idempotency token when reconnecting mid-stream instead of preserving the original token. Server treats token change as a new invocation and forwards function call again. Working on a patch to preserve token across reconnects.
investigation_notes: Reproduced with isolated harness using local webhook receiver. Issue only reproducible when stream is interrupted after first function call dispatch but before final ack for second call.
Server logs show two distinct incoming function-call events with different session-token values but identical payload bodies and timestamps separated by ~1s.
Confirmed go-sdk v0.8.7 (older) preserves session token on reconnect and does not trigger duplicate POSTs; regression introduced between v0.8.7 -> v0.9.0 where reconnect code path regenerated token.
Workaround validated: customer-side dedupe by using a composite key (order_id + customer_id) prevents duplicate shipments for now but requires app changes.
Related artifacts: pcap, server trace, and minimal repro in /tmp/brightcart-repro.zip uploaded to GH issue.
resolution_notes: In progress: SDK team authored a patch to stop regenerating session/idempotency tokens on reconnect and instead persist the original token for the life of the logical stream. Patch applied to go-sdk PR #421. We will coordinate a hotfix release (v0.9.3) and a server-side compatibility check for older clients. Post-fix regression test added to streaming test harness to simulate mid-stream reconnects.
workaround:
1) Short term: BrightCart should dedupe on their webhook endpoint by validating payload content (order_id + timestamp) to avoid duplicate shipments.
2) If they prefer, request a temporary routing rule: block duplicate payloads from same session within 5s via webhook-proxy. Support can enable a short-lived proxy rule on their Dedicated pool.
follow_up_tasks: Release go-sdk v0.9.3 with reconnect token preservation (owner: Nora Ahmed).
Backport fix to any maintained 0.9.x release branches (owner: SDK team).
Add server-side defensive dedupe: accept an optional original-session header and avoid re-executing function calls if payload hash matches (owner: Serving Runtime).
Notify BrightCart and schedule coordinated rollout for Dedicated pool (owner: Support + Account Exec).
